elements.element: Customer owns deliverables/work product created for it
elements.evidence: "any Developed Software paid for by Customer shall be the sole property of Customer"; note scope is limited to Customer-funded items and the prior sentence still says "All programs ... are and shall remain M&I's sole property".

elements.element: Vendor assigns those deliverables to Customer
elements.evidence: "M&I hereby assigns to Customer all right, title and interest in and to such Developed Software"
"M&I shall retain ownership of its pre-existing and generic software, tools, know-how and concepts"

elements.element: Perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to ANY Vendor IP embedded in deliverables
elements.evidence: licence covers only "any such M&I materials" i.e. the named categories of "pre-existing and generic software, tools, know-how and concepts", not any Vendor IP embedded in the deliverables

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data
elements.evidence: no Customer Data ownership language inserted; 17.2 left as "Customer acknowledges that it has no rights in any software, systems, documentation ... except with respect to Customer's use of the same during the Term to process its data"
ownership allocated exclusively — "sole property of Customer" / M&I "shall retain ownership"; no joint-ownership construct created

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools and know-how
elements.evidence: "M&I shall retain ownership of its pre-existing and generic software, tools, know-how and concepts"

elements.element: Customer receives perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business
elements.evidence: "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense" plus outright ownership of Customer-funded Developed Software, which subsumes the licence

offending_extra_words: or necessary for Customer's use of
Nothing in Section 17.2 shall limit Customer's rights under this Section 10.4.
reasons: Locked target is preferred, but the embedded-IP licence is narrowed to named categories of M&I materials rather than "any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables", so the preferred licence element fails.
The redline imports fallback-only rights (worldwide scope, modification and sublicensing) into a preferred-level proposal, mixing the two bargains.

No Customer Data ownership/retention language was added anywhere, and Section 17.2's blanket "no rights" acknowledgement was left intact, so the Customer Data element of the preferred position is unaddressed.

Minimality fails: the operation rewrote nearly the whole ownership passage (changed-character ratio 0.751 against the 0.600 limit) where an ownership/assignment proviso plus a short embedded-IP licence sentence would suffice, and it adds unnecessary cross-reference boilerplate ("Nothing in Section 17.2 shall limit Customer's rights ...").

Intent is not fully preserved: the existing refund/credit mechanic for Customer-funded Developed Software was deleted, and the retained sentence "All programs (including ideas and know-how and concepts) developed by M&I are and shall remain M&I's sole property" now sits in tension with Customer's ownership of Customer-funded Developed Software.
Positive note: the assignment of Customer-funded deliverables and the retention of M&I's generic tools/know-how do satisfy the fallback bargain on its material terms.
